text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers. LES ECHOS
-- Unions call demonstration on employment in Paris tomorrow.
-- Elf Aquitaine to replace Andre Tarallo as head of Elf Gabon.
-- Four Airbus [ARBU.CN] partners agree on plan keeping assets under ownership of individual partners, consortium to become a limited company with a purely management role.
-- European Union finance ministers' meeting in Luxembourg today will be the first European test for new Socialist prime minister Lionel Jospin.
-- Lyonnaise des Eaux wins water supply contract in Jakarta, Indonesia.
LA TRIBUNE
-- European partners meeting in Luxemburg are opposed to a renegotiation of the European stability pact -- France expected to seek a compromise.
-- Aerospatiale [AERP.CN] considers pulling out of the regional aircraft market.
-- Government to decide soon whether to raise the legal minimum wage SMIC, without jeopardising the current slight decrease in the number of jobseekers.
-- Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier said in an interview the company has funds to finance growth. Says British rail interests to make operating profit in 1997.
-- Merger of Worms & Cie and Saint Louis to be approved by shareholders this week.
L'AGEFI
-- Banking commission head Jean-Louis Fort calls for tighter control of terms of credit which banks offer their clients.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE

-- Aerospatiale chairman Yves Michot says merger project with Dassault is still on the agenda, expects a 20 percent rise in turnover for in 1997 to 60 billion francs, and a significant rise in profit.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- European lorry drivers on strike today for shorter working hours, expected to blockade roads and highways.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Prime Minister Lionel Jospin failed to reassure his Belgian counterpart over alternative solutions to a planned closure of the Renault Vilvoorde plant in Belgium.
